```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r packages}
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")

if (!requireNamespace("devtools", quietly = TRUE)){install.packages("devtools")}
devtools::install_github("jbisanz/qiime2R") # current version is 0.99.20
library(qiime2R)
library(tidyverse)

BiocManager::install("decontam")
library(decontam)

BiocManager::install("phyloseq")
library(phyloseq)
```

Using Qiime2R, create a phyloseq item.
```{r qiime-to-phyloseq}
##Qiime2R
physeq<-qza_to_phyloseq(
    features="table.qza",
    tree="rooted-tree.qza",
    taxonomy="taxonomy.qza",
    metadata = "Tadpole_Metadata_All_Q2.txt"
    )
physeq
```


```{r librarysize, echo = FALSE}
## Inspect Library Sizes 
df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq))
df$LibrarySize <- sample_sums(physeq)
df <- df[order(df$LibrarySize),]
df$Index <- seq(nrow(df))
ggplot(data=df, aes(x=Index, y=LibrarySize, color=Control)) + geom_point()
```


Decontam

First I will use the extraction blanks to identify contaminants. Using a threshold of 0.5, these are the taxa identified as contaminants:

```{r decontam 0.5, echo = FALSE}
# make new variable where blanks are "TRUE"
sample_data(physeq)$is.neg <- sample_data(physeq)$Control == "TRUE"

# run decontam
contamdf.prev <- isContaminant(physeq, method="prevalence", neg="is.neg", threshold=0.5)

# identify which taxa are contaminants
table(contamdf.prev$contaminant)
contams <- which(contamdf.prev$contaminant)

# list contaminants
tax <- as(tax_table(physeq), "matrix")
head(tax[contams,])
```

I will also make a plot that shows prevalence in the negatives and in true samples, to check how they are getting classified.

```{r decontam plot, echo = FALSE}
# presence-absence phyloseq for controls and samples
ps.pa <- transform_sample_counts(physeq, function(abund) 1*(abund>0))
ps.pa.neg <- prune_samples(sample_data(ps.pa)$Control == "TRUE", ps.pa)
ps.pa.pos <- prune_samples(sample_data(ps.pa)$Control == "FALSE", ps.pa)

# make dataframe for prevalence
df.pa <- data.frame(pa.pos=taxa_sums(ps.pa.pos), pa.neg=taxa_sums(ps.pa.neg),
                    contaminant=contamdf.prev$contaminant)
ggplot(data=df.pa, aes(x=pa.neg, y=pa.pos, color=contaminant)) +
  geom_point() +
  xlab("Prevalence (blanks)") +
  ylab("Prevalence (samples)") +
  ggtitle("Threshold = 0.5") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0)
```

Samples seem to split pretty cleanly into a branch that shows up mostly in positive samples, and another that shows up mostly in negative controls, and the contaminant assignment (at default probability threshold) has done a good job of identifying those mostly in negative controls. 

```{r remove contaminants, echo = FALSE}
# remove taxa from phyloseq
physeq.decontam <- prune_taxa(!contamdf.prev$contaminant, physeq)

# set up df with readcounts and % removed
readcounts <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 0, nrow = 418))
readcounts$pre <- as.data.frame(sample_sums(physeq))
readcounts$post <- sample_sums(physeq.decontam)
readcounts$per.removed <- ((readcounts$pre - readcounts$post)/readcounts$pre) *100

head(readcounts$per.removed)

# print otu table for contaminants
aqqq<-as.data.frame(otu_table(physeq)) %>% slice(contams)
```
